doc.title: Dave Bailey and John McNeil Interview, 1959-10-25

title: Father as booking agent for New Orleans bands
summary: His father booked string bands for dances near Baton Rouge, including violinist Dick Taylor.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: No, he made frequent visits to New Orleans and uh, he got a lot of his ideas from New New Orleans because you know, he used to come here and uh, he, he sort of was a, even back in those days he was sort of like a booking agent for bands out of this section from around Baton Rouge, Scotlandville and, and uh, he used to book these bands to come up to my home and play for weekend engagements and uh, and everything. So, uh, and he would make quick trips down here making contact to get bands out of here to come up that way, to play dances and things. Oh yeah.
What bands would he hire? Do you remember?

Well, he used to hire quite a few of these, and back in those days they mostly had these string bands. And uh, uh, he, one guy in particular I can remember, you know, as a kid that used to hire quite a bit, used to come and fellow with, uh, his name was Dick Taylor. He played the violin, he was real good. And uh, some of, I don't remember the names of the other guys, but in those days they used the mandolin quite a bit. And uh, as a lead instrument. And my daddy, he played the mandolin and the bass violin.
Where was Dick Taylor from? Was he from New Orleans?
He was from around this section, around Scotlandville I think mostly. Uh huh.
Oh yeah, I've been up there.
